title: nicht & kein

learn.heading: kein: "not a" / "no"
learn.text: Use **kein** to negate a noun that has **ein/eine** or **no article** at all. It takes the same endings as *ein*, and in the plural it is **keine**. In the accusative, masculine becomes **keinen**. Think of it as "ein" with a **k** in front: *ein Auto → kein Auto.*

examples.de: Haben Sie einen Einkaufswagen? – Nein, ich habe keinen.
examples.en: Do you have a shopping cart? – No, I don't have one.

examples.de: Das ist keine Wurst, das ist Käse.
examples.en: That is not sausage, that is cheese.

learn.heading: nicht: negating the rest
learn.text: Use **nicht** for everything else: verbs, adjectives, adverbs, and nouns with **der/die/das** or a possessive. Position: **at the end** of the sentence when you negate the whole sentence (*Ich kaufe das Brot nicht.*), but **before** the word you negate when it is an adjective, adverb or a place (*Das Brot ist nicht frisch. Ich wohne nicht in Aachen.*).

examples.de: Der Laden ist heute nicht geöffnet.
examples.en: The shop is not open today.

learn.heading: kein or nicht?
learn.text: Ask yourself one question: is the noun used with **ein/eine** or **without any article**? If yes, use **kein**. If the noun has **der/die/das** or **mein/dein**, use **nicht**. The answer to a question that includes a negative uses **doch** to disagree: *Du kaufst kein Brot? – Doch, ich kaufe Brot!* Do not translate "no" with *nicht* alone: "I have no time" is *Ich habe keine Zeit.*

examples.de: Ich habe heute keine Zeit zum Einkaufen.
examples.en: I have no time for shopping today.
That is not my shopping cart.

tip: Two-second test: can you put ein/eine in front of the noun, or is there no article? Then it is kein. Otherwise it is nicht. "Ich habe kein Geld" (not: nicht Geld).

children.label: kein
children.note: noun with ein or no article

exercises.explain: Bargeld is neuter and has no article → kein.
Tüte is feminine, and the noun has no definite article → keine.
Einkaufswagen is masculine and the object (accusative) → keinen.
You negate an adjective with nicht, placed before it.
The noun has the definite article das → nicht, at the end.
Geld has no article and is neuter → kein Geld.

exercises.q: "Du kaufst kein Brot?" – You want to say "Yes, I do." What do you answer?
exercises.explain: To contradict a negative question, use doch.
The adjective geöffnet is negated with nicht, before it.
Adjectives are negated with nicht: nicht teuer, nicht frisch.
kein stands directly before the noun it negates.

exercises.en: I don't have a car and I don't have time.
answer: Ich habe kein Auto und ich habe keine Zeit
Ich habe kein Auto und keine Zeit
exercises.explain: Both nouns come with ein/no article, so kein (neuter Auto) and keine (feminine Zeit).
